Agathangelos, History of the Armenians (Patmut'iwn Hayots'), 5th c. CE; trans. Robert W. Thomson (SUNY Press, Albany, 1976)

Reused: the standard 5th-c. account of the conversion of Armenia under King Tiridates III and Gregory the Illuminator; primary attestation for Gregory, Tiridates, and the founding of the Armenian Apostolic Church.
Movses Khorenatsi, History of Armenia (Patmut'iwn Hayots'), 5th c. CE; trans. Robert W. Thomson (Harvard University Press, Cambridge MA, 1978)
Reused: 5th-c. Armenian national history written within the circle of Mashtots and Sahak; primary attestation for Mesrop Mashtots's invention of the alphabet, Sahak Partev, and Nerses the Great.
James R. Russell, Zoroastrianism in Armenia (Harvard Iranian Series 5, 1987)

Reused here for the pre-Christian-to-Christian transition: documents the replacement of the Iranian/Zoroastrian yazata cult (Aramazd etc.) by the Christianity established under Tiridates and Gregory the Illuminator.
Gregory of Narek, The Book of Lamentations (Matean Voghbergut'ean / Narek), c. 1002-1003 CE; trans. Thomas J. Samuelian, Speaking with God from the Depths of the Heart (Vem Press, Yerevan, 2002)

The masterwork of Armenian Christian mysticism: 95 prayer-poems of penitential dialogue with God. Primary attestation for Gregory of Narek as mystic-poet of the Narek monastery (Vaspurakan), proclaimed a Doctor of the Universal Church in 2015.
